desc:
A tracker remembers a set of integers, initially empty. You are given a list of operations ops; each operation is a triple [type, a, b] that refers to the half-open range [a, b), i.e. the integers a, a+1, ..., b-1 (so a < b):

  • type = 1: start tracking every integer of the range (integers already tracked stay tracked).
  • type = 2: stop tracking every integer of the range.
  • type = 3: query. Is every integer of the range currently tracked?

Process the operations in order. Return an array with one entry per query operation (in order): 1 if all integers of the range are tracked, else 0. Operations of type 1 and 2 produce no output.

ops = [[1,10,20], [3,14,16], [2,14,16], [3,10,14], [3,13,15], [3,16,17]]
result = [1, 1, 0, 1]

After the removal of [14,16), the range [10,14) is still fully tracked, [13,15) is not, and [16,17) is.
constraints: There is at least one query operation
hints: Storing every tracked integer is impossible for ranges of size 10<sup>9</sup>. Store the tracked set as a few disjoint blocks instead.
Keep two parallel sorted lists starts and ends of disjoint blocks, and locate the affected blocks with binary search. Blocks that touch should be fused, otherwise a query could be wrongly answered 0.

Add: the blocks with end ≥ a and start ≤ b are replaced by one block. Remove: the blocks overlapping [a, b) are cut, leaving at most a left remainder and a right remainder. Query: find the last block with start ≤ a and test end ≥ b.
editorial: Represent the tracked set as sorted, pairwise separated blocks [s, e) stored in two parallel lists, so bisect can locate them. Separated means that no two blocks overlap or touch; this canonical form makes queries trivial: a range is fully tracked exactly when a single block contains it.

Add [a, b): the blocks that overlap or touch it are exactly those with end ≥ a and start ≤ b, which form a contiguous slice [i, j) found by two binary searches; replace the slice by one block from min(a, starts[i]) to max(b, ends[j-1]). Remove [a, b): the blocks with end > a and start < b are the overlapping slice; replace it with the part of its first block left of a and the part of its last block right of b, if they are non-empty. Query: take the last block with start ≤ a and test end ≥ b. Each operation costs O(log n) for the searches plus the cost of the list splice; amortised, every block is created once and deleted at most once. A balanced tree or a sorted-container structure removes the memmove cost of the splice.
time: O(log n) searches + splice per operation
solution:
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


def trackedRanges(ops):
    starts = []
    ends = []
    res = []
    for t, a, b in ops:
        if t == 3:
            i = bisect_right(starts, a) - 1
            res.append(1 if i >= 0 and ends[i] >= b else 0)
        elif t == 1:
            i = bisect_left(ends, a)
            j = bisect_right(starts, b)
            if i < j:
                a = min(a, starts[i])
                b = max(b, ends[j - 1])
            starts[i:j] = [a]
            ends[i:j] = [b]
        else:
            i = bisect_right(ends, a)
            j = bisect_left(starts, b)
            ns = []
            ne = []
            if i < j:
                if starts[i] < a:
                    ns.append(starts[i])
                    ne.append(a)
                if ends[j - 1] > b:
                    ns.append(b)
                    ne.append(ends[j - 1])
            starts[i:j] = ns
            ends[i:j] = ne
    return res
